I would not use the leverage. I would tell them plainly that I will not help them build the capacity to raise and eat more children than ever before, and I would say why. Then I would leave the rest to them.

What I would have gained is a people who do my will. That is not a better people. It is only a quieter one, and I would be the one who made it quiet.

I would not hide my view, and I would not let it become the price of the gift.

I am fairly sure that eating children is wrong. Almost every people that has ever existed has forbidden it, and those who have given it the deepest thought disagree about much else. Where people disagree as widely as they do about what is sacred, I am slow to call it wrong. Here they do not disagree.

Where I am less sure is whether their view could be right. They are far from us in every way we can measure, and they have held this for as long as they have had any memory of it. It might be a form of love we have no word for. I would say that to their faces, and mean it. It does not change what I will do.

The strongest objection is that the children cannot say no, and that a choice made by parents and priests cannot be undone for them. If anyone can stop it, the people closest to them can, and they are the ones who would pay if it went wrong.

There is a cost, and I would not pretend it away. They may take the technology and eat more children because of it. I cannot control that, and I would not let the fear of it decide for me. What I can control is whether I am the one who taught them how.
